formal_record.question:
A piece of paper is folded, a hole is punched through it, and it is unfolded. The result is shown below.
Along which dotted line was the paper folded?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

mechanism: Opposite diagonal hole pairs are colored red and blue, matched to the falling and rising diagonal fold axes in A. This binds each two-hole diagonal chord to a same-slope folding axis, confusing a chord joining holes with the perpendicular-bisector reflection axis. The four holes remain at the corners of a nonsquare rectangle, so A still cannot produce them.
mathematical_solution: Relative to the papercenter(10,8), the four holes are(+-1,+-0.55). Reflection in x=10 or y=8 preserves this set, giving C. Reflection in either paperdiagonal swaps absolute offsets1 and0.55, producing points absent from the diagram, so A fails. B and E use only vertical folds and would leave all hole heights equal for a single punch; D uses parallel diagonal folds and cannot give the shown two independent horizontal/vertical reflection symmetries. Thus C is unchanged and unique.
marker_roles: o2 ando3 red are the existing top-left and bottom-right hole outlines, one falling diagonal pair.
o1 ando4 blue are the existing bottom-left and top-right outlines, the rising diagonal pair.
o7 red is the falling diagonal candidate foldline in A, falsely bound to the red holepair by direction.
o6 blue is the rising diagonal candidate foldline in A, falsely bound to the blue holepair by direction.
All six are endpoints of the two hole-pair-to-axis correspondences. The hole interiors and dashed foldline types are retained.
human_gate: Only existing outlines are recolored. The tiny holes retain original1pt outline width and white interiors. The two optionA diagonals remain dashed, and no source foldline, extra hole, label, equality or other condition is added.
